literal: Without moving far away, without approaching too close, like those who warm themselves by fire, let those who associate with and conduct themselves before mighty kings be.
translation: Let those who associate with mighty kings conduct themselves like people warming themselves by a fire—neither staying too far away, nor drawing too close.
modern: வலிமைமிக்க அரசர்களுடன் பழகி வாழ்பவர்கள், நெருப்பில் குளிர் காய்வோரைப் போல, மிகத் தூரத்திலும் விலகாமல், மிக அருகிலும் நெருங்காமல் பக்குவமாக நடந்து கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet advises ministers and courtiers on how to maintain a safe and respectful relationship with powerful rulers. It uses the vivid analogy of warming oneself by a fire. If you stand too far away, you do not receive its warmth; if you get too close, you get burned. Similarly, being too distant from a king leads to neglect, while being too familiar or close can provoke anger and ruin. The word 'ikal' here highlights the formidable power of the king, which must be treated with constant caution.
